pending.why: BACKLOG (6 findings): the rule modules are grouped by what they measure - Height, Naming, Nesting, Size, Width - which puts them two segments below the package root, where this rule recognises only `<Pkg>.<Name>` and `<Pkg>.Data.<Name>` as public. The grouping is right; it is the rule's list of allowed namespaces that is incomplete. Same complaint as gig-pilot's `Service.Source.*`, `Service.Http.*` and `Web.TsBridge.*`, so this is one decision across three repositories - which sub-namespaces count as public - and not five separate exemptions.
BACKLOG (5 findings): expressions built inline where a `let` would name the inner part.
BACKLOG (2 findings): `maybe`/`fromMaybe` given arguments that have to be built, where a `case` reads better.
BACKLOG (2 findings): a combinator spread over more than one line, which is the point at which a `case` is clearer.
BACKLOG (3 findings): guards where two branches would read as an if/else.
BACKLOG (2 findings): calls nested deeper than the max, wanting intermediate names.
BACKLOG (1 finding): arms disagreeing about whether the body follows `->` or starts on the next line.
BACKLOG (1 finding): a block nested directly inside a block of the same kind, which flattens.
BACKLOG (1 finding): a `where` clause, where this style uses `let` so bindings read in the order they are needed.

BACKLOG (1 finding): 170 characters of guidance prose held as a string literal. The rule's own hint says where it goes - this module's trailing comment - so this one has a known fix rather than a judgement call.
